input:
Derivative of tan⁻¹( (√(1+x²) - √(1-x²)) / (√(1+x²) + √(1-x²)) ) w.r.t. cos⁻¹(x²) is

Options:
A. -1/2
B. -1
C. 1/2
D. 1

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Find dy/dz where y = tan⁻¹( (√(1+x²) - √(1-x²)) / (√(1+x²) + √(1-x²)) ) and z = cos⁻¹(x²).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute x² = cos(2θ). Then z = 2θ, so θ = z/2. Simplifying y gives y = π/4 - θ = π/4 - z/2. Thus dy/dz = -1/2 directly.

key_concepts: Parametric differentiation / derivative of one function w.r.t another
Identities: √(1 + cos 2θ) = √2 cos θ, √(1 - cos 2θ) = √2 sin θ
tan⁻¹((cos θ - sin θ)/(cos θ + sin θ)) = tan⁻¹(tan(π/4 - θ)) = π/4 - θ

key_formulas.substitution: x² = cos(2θ) ⇒ z = cos⁻¹(x²) = 2θ ⇒ θ = z/2
key_formulas.y_simplified: y = tan⁻¹((1 - tan θ)/(1 + tan θ)) = π/4 - θ = π/4 - z/2

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute x² = cos(2θ) into both y and z expressions, simplify y to a linear function of z, and differentiate directly.
logical_steps: Step 1: Set x² = cos(2θ), which gives z = cos⁻¹(cos 2θ) = 2θ
Step 2: Simplify √(1+x²) = √2 cos θ and √(1-x²) = √2 sin θ
Step 3: Substitute into y: tan⁻¹((√2 cos θ - √2 sin θ)/(√2 cos θ + √2 sin θ))
Step 4: Divide numerator and denominator by √2 cos θ: tan⁻¹((1 - tan θ)/(1 + tan θ)) = π/4 - θ
Step 5: Replace θ = z/2: y = π/4 - z/2
Step 6: Compute dy/dz = -1/2 and match option

step_3_simplify_y.fraction: (√2 cos θ - √2 sin θ) / (√2 cos θ + √2 sin θ) = (cos θ - sin θ) / (cos θ + sin θ)
step_3_simplify_y.divide_by_cos: = (1 - tan θ) / (1 + tan θ) = tan(π/4 - θ)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Since y = π/4 - z/2, dy/dz is simply -1/2 ✓
